title: scene-plan.json
description: Deterministic mapping of each script scene to a render component + props. Replaces the old human-gated storyboard (fixed templates → no gate).

audio.description: OPTIONAL sound design (D-063) — tracks mixed ALONGSIDE the narration, which remains the one continuous track that is never cut. Files come from the shared assets/sfx/ library, so a riser bought once is reused on every hero moment. A missing file is a warning and the cue is dropped: sound design never kills a render.

bed.description: A quiet music bed under the whole video, looped.

gain.description: Keep it low — the voice normalizes to -16 LUFS and nothing here is side-chain ducked.

sfx.description: One-shot cues placed on the NARRATION clock (the same clock as alignment.json), snapped to a frame here.

atSeconds.description: Narration-clock seconds, as read off alignment.json.

items.description: Either a single template+props, OR a `beats` array to split one script scene into several timed visuals (D-022).

engine.description: OPTIONAL render engine for this scene (default remotion). Set 'hyperframes' to route a single hero beat to a pre-rendered silent HyperFrames clip composited at the scene window (V6). Surgical — 1–3 per video at most.

props.description: Component props. Optional MOTIVATED-MOTION (opt-in, surgical — never global): `focalZoom`: { target:{x,y} (0..1), scale (<=~1.6), in/out (narration cue words) } punches into a target on cue and releases; `pip`: { anchor:'top-right'|'top-left', content, in/out } shows a corner inset. build-props resolves cue words to scene-local frames. Use ONLY for single-focus content (capture-segment, code-block, stat-callout, prompt cards) — NOT tables/lists/body text.

revealOn.description: Reveal sub-elements at each of this scene's sentence starts.

cueWords.description: Reveal sub-element i when this word is spoken.

beats.description: Split the scene into ordered visual beats; each covers a slice of the scene's sentences.

props.description: Component props. Optional MOTIVATED-MOTION (opt-in, surgical — never global): `focalZoom`: { target:{x,y} (0..1), scale (<=~1.6), in/out (narration cue words) } punches into a target on cue and releases; `pip`: { anchor:'top-right'|'top-left', content, in/out } shows a corner inset. build-props resolves cue words to scene-local frames. Use ONLY for single-focus content (capture-segment, code-block, stat-callout, prompt cards) — NOT tables/lists/body text.

transitionOut.description: How this scene EXITS into the next one (D-060). Default `cut` — the cut lands exactly on the narration beat. MECHANIZED: `cut` (windows abut), `dissolve` (opacity cross-blend over the crossfade), `push` (the incoming scene slides in as this one slides out). AUTHORIAL — recorded and reviewable, but compiled as a hard CUT because the compositor cannot align two independently pre-rendered scenes: `match`, `morph`, `carry`. Those three are a CONTRACT WITH THE AUTHOR: compose the two adjacent scenes so their frames rhyme, then let the cut do the work. On a scene with `beats`, the scene-level value governs the LAST beat's exit; inner beat boundaries default to `cut` unless the beat sets its own. The LAST scene's value is ignored (it cross-blends with the outro bumper) — build-props warns.

direction.description: The art-direction brief for this scene: prose FOR THE AUTHOR of the visual, never for the renderer. INERT BY CONTRACT — `direction` is deliberately kept out of timeline.json, so it never reaches the HyperFrames jobVariables and therefore cannot enter the HF render cache key. That is what makes a typo fix in `premise` free instead of a full re-render of the clip. Anything the RENDERER must obey is a new field next to `transitionOut` (the executable side), never a field in here.

premise.description: What this scene is DOING for the viewer, and how it looks/moves — the idea a bespoke HyperFrames scene is written from.

palette.description: Colour intent for this scene (e.g. 'black + gold hero', 'blue + gold body').

carry.description: The element that must survive the boundary into the next scene — the author's half of a `match`/`morph`/`carry` transitionOut.
